title: Jordan National Policy Intelligence Platform
summary: A production-grade multi-agent system for querying Arabic legal and policy documents in natural language, where every answer carries citations and a confidence score.
problem: Jordanian government bodies needed a way to search and query large volumes of Arabic legal and policy documents using natural language — instead of manual document review, users needed grounded, citable answers they could trust for government-level decision-making.

approach.heading: Multi-agent architecture
body: Built as a production-grade multi-agent AI system with an enterprise-style microservices architecture — 5 services separating concerns across knowledge management, governance, workflow orchestration, agent services, and frontend integration.
Each agent handles a distinct part of the query pipeline.

approach.heading: Grounding and traceability
body: Every AI response is grounded with citations and confidence scoring, so answers are traceable back to source documents rather than presented as unverified generation.

approach.heading: Built for production
body: The system was designed with scalability and production deployment in mind from the start, not just as a prototype.

contribution: Contributed to the platform's pipeline to make it production-ready for government-scale use.
Independently developed and integrated the React-based frontend — the primary interface through which users interact with the multi-agent system and view grounded, cited responses.
outcome: Delivered a working, cited-response system for querying Arabic legal and policy documents — a domain where accuracy and traceability matter more than raw generation speed.
learnings: Working across 5 microservices reinforced how to design AI systems where trust (citations, confidence scores) is a first-class architectural requirement, not an afterthought — a principle I now carry into every AI product I build.
